Condition : 1 - The development hereby permitted shall be begun within 3 years from the date of this permission.

Reason: To accord with the provisions of Section 92 (1) of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990.
Condition : 2 - The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and specifications: [3901E-LB-TR-00-D-A-101000 Rev C02, 3901E-LB-TR-00-D-A-101001 Rev C02, 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-130000 Rev C02, 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-140000 Rev C02, 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-140001 Rev C02, 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-300000 Rev C02, 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-300003 Rev C02, 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-300001 Rev C02, 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-300002 Rev C02, Arboricultural Report Rev 1 (dated 5 July 2024), Arboricultural Report Rev 1 (dated 9 July 2024), Air Quality Technical Memorandum (dated 10 July 2024), Daylight and Sunlight Report (dated August 2024), Design and Access Statement (dated July 2024), Energy Statement Rev A (dated July 2024), Fire Safety Statement [Ref: OF-001804-FSS-05-A] (dated 16 July 2024), Location Plan (dated 9 August 2024), Noise Impact Assessment Rev 1 (dated 25 July 2024), Outline Construction Logistics Plan Rev 1 (dated 26 June 2024), Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (PEA) Rev 1 (dated 2 August 2024), Preliminary Land Quality Risk Assessment Rev 1, Transport Statement Rev 1 (dated 28 June 2024) and Preliminary Land Quality Risk Assessment (PLQRA) Rev 1 (dated 11 July 2024). Received 09/08/2024; Drainage Strategy Rev 2 (dated 6 March 2025). Received 06/03/2025; 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-130001 Rev C03, 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-130002 Rev C03 and 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-130003 Rev C03. Received 25/04/2025; Transport Technical Note Rev 1. Received 09/07/2025; 3901E-LB-TR-00-D-A-110000 Rev C04, 3901E-LB-TR-00-D-A-120000 Rev C04, 3901E-LB-TR-01-D-A-120001 Rev C03, 3901E-LB-TR-02-D-A-120002 Rev C02, 3901E-LB-TR-RF-D-A-120003 Rev C03 and 3901E-LB-TR-00-DP-L-200000 Rev P04. Received 24/07/2025; Highway Register Site Overlay. Received 29/07/2025].

Reason: In order to ensure the development is carried out in accordance with the planning permission.
Condition : 3 - Materials

Prior to above ground works (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant shall have submitted to the Local Planning Authority, for approval in writing, details and samples of the materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the development hereby permitted. The samples/details shall include:

-	Brick/stone coping (including protruding and recessed brick detail, soldier coursing, mortar colours, joint type, stretcher bond and sample panels a minimum size of 1m x 1m);
-	Tiles, balustrades/railings and metalwork;
-	Doors and window treatments (including sections and reveals) and;
-	Any other materials/details to be used.

The development shall not be carried out otherwise than in accordance with the approved details and maintained as such thereafter.

Reason: In order to safeguard the appearance of the area.
Condition : 4 - Landscaping works

Notwithstanding the details on the approved plans, a scheme detailing site-wide hard and soft landscaping for the relevant area of the site as set out in the approved drawings shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority prior to the occupation of the hereby approved development. The detailed landscaping scheme shall include the following details:

�	Soft planting: including any grass and turf areas, trees, planters, shrub and herbaceous areas including details of species, sizes and numbers/densities;
�	Hard landscaping: including ground surfaces, kerbs, edges, ridge and;
�	Flexible pavings, unit paving, tree pit root barriers, furniture, steps, 'visual thread' and if;
�	Fences and walls and any other boundary treatments;
�	Any signage and information boards;
�	Any external lighting and;
�	Any other landscaping feature(s) forming part of the scheme.

The submission shall include a management programme for the lifetime of the development.

Any trees or shrubs planted which die within five years of completion of the development shall be replaced with the same species, and of comparable maturity, or an approved alternative.

The development shall be carried out strictly in accordance with the details so approved and shall be maintained as such thereafter.

Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions and to ensure a satisfactory appearance of the site and area.
Condition : 5 - Boundary treatment

Prior to the occupation of the hereby approved development the boundary treatments shall be erected in strict accordance with the approved plans and Design and Access Statement.

Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions and to ensure a satisfactory appearance.
Condition : 6 - Energy strategy

No development shall take place until the applicant has entered into a binding arrangement with the Council that will secure a suitable contribution to the Council's Carbon Offset Fund, in accordance with the zero-carbon strategy set out in the Energy Statement hereby approved.

Prior to first occupation of any dwelling within the development hereby approved evidence (e.g. photographs, installation contracts and As-Built certificates under the Standard Assessment Procedure) shall be submitted to the Local Planning Authority and approved in writing to show that the development has been constructed in accordance with the approved Energy Strategy and any subsequent approved revisions.

Reason: In order to ensure that the development makes the fullest contribution to minimising carbon dioxide emissions.
Condition : 7 - Water efficiency

Prior to first occupation of the building(s) hereby approved, the development shall have been constructed to achieve an internal water use of 105 litres/person/day or less.

Reason: In order to protect and conserve water supplies and resources.
Condition : 8 - Sustainable sourcing of materials

The development hereby approved shall not be occupied until evidence (e.g. photographs and copies of delivery notes, invoices or installation contracts) have been submitted to the Local Planning Authority to demonstrate that the development meets the following:

At least three of the key elements of the building envelope (external walls, windows roof, upper floor slabs, internal walls, floor finishes/coverings) are to achieve a rating of A+ to D in the Building Research Establishment (BRE) The Green Guide of specification.

At least 50% of timber and timber products are to be sourced from accredited Forest Stewardship Council (FSC) or Programme for the Endorsement of Forestry Certification (PEFC) scheme.

No construction or insulation materials are to be used which will release toxins into the internal and external environment, including those that deplete stratospheric ozone.

Reason: In the interests of sustainable development and in order to ensure the sustainable sourcing of materials.
Condition : 9 - Obscure windows

The windows serving bathrooms formed in the east (rear) elevation on the first and second floors of the hereby approved development as shown on drawing numbers 3901E-LB-TR-01-D-A-120001 Rev C03, 3901E-LB-TR-02-D-A-120002 Rev C02 and 3901E-LB-TR-ZZ-D-A-130002 Rev C03 shall be obscure glazed, hinged to open inwards and shall not be repaired or replaced otherwise than with obscured glazing.

Reason: In order to protect the privacy of future occupiers and neighbours'.
Condition : 10 - Construction Logistics Plan

Prior to commencement of development, a Construction Logistics Plan, written in accordance with the latest TfL guidance or a subsequent version, related to that phase shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Construction Logistics Plan shall include:

a)	A site plan (showing the elements set out below);

b)	Confirmation that a pre-start record of site conditions on the adjoining public highway will be undertaken with Hounslow Highways and a commitment to repair any damage caused;

c)	Provision for the parking of vehicles of site operatives and visitors;

d)	Provisions for loading, unloading and storage of plant and materials within the site;

e)	Details of access to the site, including means to control and manage access and egress of vehicles to and from the site for the duration of construction including phasing arrangements;

f)	Details of vehicle routeing from the site to the wider strategic road network;

g)	The erection and maintenance of security hoarding including decorative displays and facilities for public viewing, where appropriate;

h)	Provision of wheel washing facilities at the site exit and a commitment to sweep adjacent roads when required and at the request of the Council;

i)	A scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works;

j)	Measures to ensure the safety of all users of the public highway especially cyclists and pedestrians in the vicinity of the site and especially at the access;

k)	Commitment to liaise with other contractors in the vicinity of the site to maximise the potential for consolidation and to minimise traffic impacts;

l)	Avoidance of peak hours for deliveries and details of a booking system to avoid vehicles waiting on the access road;

m)	All necessary traffic orders and other permissions required to allow safe access to the site to be secured and implemented prior to commencement of constru
Condition : 11 - Car Park Management Plan

Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, a Parking Management Plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall include the following:

I.	Details of parking allocations for residents of the approved development and how this will be operated and enforced;

II.	Details of measures proposed to restrict parking to designated bays only and prohibit parking on the access road;

III.	Details of electric vehicle charging and a commitment to convert passive EV bays to active when demand requires;

IV.	Measures to ensure that all prospective residents are informed of the Parking Management Plan.

The parking area and access road shall thereafter be managed in compliance with the approved Parking Management Plan, unless the prior written approval of the local planning authority is obtained to secure any variation.

Reason: In order to promote sustainable modes of transport, to protect neighbours' living conditions and to ensure minimal disruption of traffic in the locality.
Condition : 12 - Reinstate footway

Before the development hereby permitted is first occupied or brought into use, the existing vehicular access (to the front of the site) along Tivoli Road shall be permanently closed and the kerbs and footway reinstated so that it cannot be used as an access across the pavement.

Reason: In order to enhance the pedestrian environment and to confine vehicular access to the permitted points in order to ensure that the development does not prejudice the free flow of traffic or highway safety along the adjacent highway.
Condition : 13 - New vehicular access

Either side of the vehicle access hereby approved, visibility splay areas (the depth measured from the back of the footway and the widths outwards from the edges of the access, with a splay of at least 2.4 metres x 2.4 metres) shall be provided before the access and parking area is brought into use. These areas shall be kept clear of any obstructions to visibility greater than 600 mm in height, including shrubs, planting, boundary walls, fences, gates, other means of enclosure or other structures or objects at all times. A minimum 1.2m wide and clear pedestrian access route shall be made available and shall thereafter be retained as such, without obstruction, for the lifetime of the development.

Reason: To ensure adequate visibility for drivers entering and leaving the site in the interests of pedestrian and vehicle safety.
Condition : 14 - Delivery and Servicing Plan

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until, a Delivery & Servicing Plan has been submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The Plan shall provide details to how deliveries and servicing will be undertaken within the site and the measures proposed to restrict loading and unloading on the public highway. The development shall be implemented in accordance with the approved delivery and servicing plan (or any variation approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority) and shall be maintained as such for the lifetime of the development.

Reason: In the interests of the safety of pedestrians and vehicles and to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 15 - Cycle parking

Notwithstanding the submitted details and prior to occupation of the development hereby approved, full details (including manufacturers specifications) of secure, covered, cycle parking facilities (for not less than 10 bicycles) for the occupants of, and visitors to, the development shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority.

The approved facilities shall be fully implemented and made available for use before any part of the development is first occupied and thereafter retained for use at all times without obstruction.

Reason: In order to support sustainable transport objectives.
Condition : 16 - Refuse and recycling storage

Prior to first occupation of the development hereby approved, the refuse and recycling storage shown on the approved drawings numbered 3901E-LB-TR-00-D-A-120000 Rev C04 and 3910E-LB-TR-00-DP-L-200000 Rev P04and shall be made available for use in strict accordance with the approved plans and shall thereafter be retained as such, without obstruction, for the lifetime of the development.

Reason: In order to ensure adequate provision for waste and recycling.
Condition : 17 - Land quality - intrusive site investigation 

Prior to commencement (excluding site investigation and demolition) of the development hereby approved:

Following the completion of the Phase I desk study report, if intrusive investigations or gas monitoring is recommended, a Phase II site investigation must be undertaken.

No development other than necessary works to enable intrusive investigations shall take place until a Phase II site investigation report, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.
This report shall identify the areas and sources of land contamination that exist on the site and identify the scope of site remediation measures necessary before the development commences.

The investigation shall be carried out by a competent person(s), based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations, to identify the extent and nature of contaminants. The initial CSM shall be updated accordingly following a tiered risk assessment based on the findings of the investigation, and where applicable, the report shall include proposals to deal with the identified contamination on site.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.

Supporting Notes:

I.	The report shall include details of such sampling of soil, soil vapour, ground gas, leachate, surface water and/or groundwater at such locations and depths as are considered to characterise the site conditions based on the initial Conceptual Site Model (CSM) and on-site observations during investigation work.

II.	The investigation and the report must adhere to current UK guidance and best practice.

III.	Further investigation shall be carried out at such locations and at such depths as the local plan
Condition : 18 - Land quality - Remediation Method Statement/ Remediation Strategy 

Prior to commencement (excluding site investigation and demolition) of the development hereby approved:

If a scheme for remediation is recommended in the Phase II site investigation for the site, no development shall take place until a remediation method statement prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person to specify the works necessary to render the site suitable for its proposed end use, has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.

Supporting Notes:

I.	The remediation method statement shall provide suitable details of how the risks of each pollutant linkages, as identified in the updated Conceptual Site Model, will be mitigated.

II.	The report shall account for any comments made by the local planning authority.

III.	Remediation work shall be carried out in accordance with the approved remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.

IV.	The Council requests that remediation method statement or site plans be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 19 - Land quality - additional/unexpected contamination found during development

During the development:

The Local Planning Authority shall be notified immediately if any land contamination not previously identified is encountered during development. A competent person shall assess the contamination, where necessary, including soil and groundwater sampling and testing before any further part of the development that may be affected by the additional contamination that has been discovered continues.

A revised remediation method statement, prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person, shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval within one month of the discovery of such contamination.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.

Supporting notes:

I.	Further remediation work to remove or manage additional contamination shall be carried out in accordance with the approved revised remediation method statement for verification and validation before the development is first brought into use.

II.	In some instances, the local planning authority may require work on site to be ceased whilst the nature of additional contamination is investigated fully.

III.	The Council requests that the revised remediation method statement or any site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 20 - Land quality - verification and validation of remedial work 

Prior to the development is first brought into use:

The agreed scheme for remediation, including any amendments, shall be fully implemented. A verification report produced upon completion of the remediation by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person shall be submitted in writing to the local planning authority for approval, before the development is first brought into use or in accordance with a programme approved in writing by the local planning authority.

Reason: Contamination is known or suspected on the site due to a former land use. It is therefore necessary to ensure that the development can be implemented and occupied with adequate regard for public and environmental safety.

Supporting notes:

I.	The verification (closure) report shall revisit the conceptual site model and provide evidence that each aspect of the remediation plan has been implemented correctly and successfully in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice. Where applicable, the report shall describe how any additional/unexpected contamination encountered during development has been managed in line with the revised remediation method statement.

II.	This report shall demonstrate that the development is suitable for its proposed use in terms of land quality.

III.	The Council requests that the verification report or site photos be sent electronically to landquality@hounslow.gov.uk as well as being submitted to the local planning authority for approval.
Condition : 21 - Land quality - long term monitoring and maintenance 

If long term monitoring and maintenance is required following successful completion of approved remedial measures, reports which demonstrate the effectiveness of the monitoring and maintenance shall be prepared by a suitably qualified, experienced or supervised person and submitted to the local planning authority according to an agreed timescale as shall first have been approved under other conditions set out in this planning approval decision notice.

This shall be conducted in accordance with current UK guidance and best practice.

Reason: In order to ensure that risks from land contamination to the future users of the land and neighbouring land are minimised, together with those to controlled waters, properties and ecological systems.
Condition : 22 - Drainage design 

Prior to commencement of groundworks (excluding site investigations and demolition), the applicant must submit a final detailed drainage design including drawings and supporting calculations [and updated Drainage Assessment Form] to the Lead Local Flood Authority for review and approval, aligned with the Drainage Strategy (06/03/2025) and associated drawings. The drainage hierarchy shall make use of green infrastructure technology to comply with the hierarchy set out in London Plan Policy SI 13. A detailed management plan confirming routine maintenance tasks for all drainage components must also be submitted to demonstrate how the drainage system is to be maintained for the lifetime of the development. A maintenance owner should be provided.

Reason: In order to prevent the risk of flooding to and from the site.
Condition : 23 - Built in accordance with drainage details 

The building hereby permitted shall not be occupied until evidence (photographs and installation contracts) is submitted to demonstrate that the sustainable drainage scheme for the site has been completed in accordance with the submitted details. The sustainable drainage scheme shall be managed and maintained thereafter in accordance with the agreed management and maintenance plan for all of the proposed drainage components.

Reason: In order to ensure that the methods to mitigate the risk of surface water flooding have been implemented as agreed and that the drainage system is suitably managed.
Condition : 24 - Lighting

Artificial lighting as part of the completed development shall be designed to meet the Obtrusive Light Limitations for Exterior Lighting Installations for Environmental Zone - E2 set out in Table 2 of the Institute of Lighting Engineers Guidance Notes for the Reduction of Obtrusive Light, 01/21 (https://theilp.org.uk/publication/guidance-note-1-for-the-reduction-of-obtrusive-light-2021/) or such other guidance as may supersede it. The installation shall be examined by a lighting engineer affiliated to a nationally recognised body that specialises in the field of external lighting and certified to confirm that it complies with this standard before it is first brought into use and a copy of the certificate supplied to the local planning authority to confirm compliance before the lights are first brought into operation.

Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions.
Condition : 25 - Design Out Crime

The development shall achieve 'Secured by Design' accreditation awarded by the Design-Out Crime Officer from the Metropolitan Police Service on behalf of the Association of Chief Police Officers (ACPO).

No dwelling shall be occupied until accreditation has been achieved and evidence of such accreditation has been submitted to the local planning authority.

Reason: In pursuance of the Council's duty under section 17 of the Crime and Disorder Act 1998.
Condition : 26 - All Non-road Mobile Machinery (NRMM)

All Non-Road Mobile Machinery (NRMM) of net power of 37kW and up to and including 560kW used during the course of the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development hereby approved shall comply with the emission standards set out in chapter 7 of the GLA's supplementary planning guidance (SPG) 'Control of Dust and Emissions During Construction and Demolition' dated July 2014, or subsequent guidance. Unless it complies with the standards set out in the SPG, no NRMM shall be on site, at any time, whether in use or not. The developer shall keep an up to date list of all NRMM used during the demolition, site preparation and construction phases of the development on the online register at https://nrmm.london/.

The development shall also demonstrate that the proposed development is complaint with Building Emissions Benchmark (BEBs), specified in the GLA's Supplementary Planning Guidance "Sustainable Design and Construction" dated April 2014).

Reason: To minimise air pollution in the interests of air quality and the wider local environment.
Condition : 27 - Fixed Plant

The cumulative noise from any fixed external plant associated with the scheme should not exceed levels more than 10 dB below representative background (LA90) levels at free field locations representing facades of nearby existing and proposed dwellings. Noise levels should be assessed by measurement or calculation based on the guidance presented within BS4142: 2014+A1:2019 or subsequent versions of this guidance.

Reason: In order to ensure that existing and proposed residential units are not exposed to unreasonable levels fixed plant noise.
Condition : 28 - Internal and external noise criteria

Maximum noise levels permitted within the dwellings will not exceed those that are specified in Table 4 of British Standard 8233:2014 [Living Rooms = 35 dB LAeq, 16 hours; Dining room/area = 40 dB LAeq, 16 hours; Bedroom = 35 dB LAeq, 16 hours during day-time (07:00 - 23:00) and Bedroom = 30 dB LAeq, 8 hours during night-time (23:00 - 07:00), night-time (23:00 � 07:00) LAmax noise levels within bedrooms do not exceed 45 dB LAmax more than 10 to 15 times per night. All occupiers should have access to amenity spaces where noise levels do not exceed 50dB LAeq,16hours.

Reason: In order to protect future occupiers from unacceptable noise levels.
Condition : 29 - Construction Noise Limits

Based upon guidance contained within BS 5228:2009 + A1:2014: Noise, Noise levels from construction works at nearby existing and proposed residential receptors shall not exceed the following construction noise criteria:

�	Daytime works will not exceed 75 dB LAeq,T at the worst-affected residential property during the following time periods:
�	Monday to Friday (08:00 � 18:00 hours)
�	Saturday (08:00 to 13:00 hours)

Works outside of the standard hours will be subject to prior agreement and prior notice will be provided to the London Borough of Hounslow.

Reason: In order to protect neighbours' living conditions.
Condition : 30 - Stopping Up Order

Prior to the commencement of development, the area of highway land to the front of the existing access on Tivoli Road shall be subject to a Stopping Up Order under Section 247 of the Town and Country Planning Act 1990 (or other relevant legislation), to remove its status as Public Highway. No development shall take place until an application for the Stopping Up Order has been confirmed and no part of the development hereby permitted shall be occupied until the Stopping Up Order has been implemented in full. All costs associated with the application and implementation of the Stopping Up Order shall be met by the applicant.

Reason: In order to protect the appearance of the and in the interests of highway safety.
Condition : 31 - Ecological Management Plan

Notwithstanding the details in the approved Preliminary Ecological Appraisal (PEA) Rev 1 (dated 2 August 2024), no development shall take place, including any works of demolition, until dusk and dawn emergence surveys for bats (including an internal building inspection) have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority.

The surveys shall be carried out in line with Bat Conservation Trust (BCT) Bat Survey Good Practice Guidelines (Collins, 2016) and any scheme of protection/mitigation shall be carried out in accordance with the approved details.

Reason: In the interest of biodiversity.
description: Erection of a three storey block consisting of 6 self contained flats with associated landscaping, private amenity space, car parking, cycle and refuse storage following the demolition of the existing garages.
